metadata.purpose: The twelve precessional ages as prose, for LLM-friendly chronological reference.

data.title: The twelve precessional ages
data.prose: The corpus organizes its long-form content around the twelve precessional ages of one Great Year. Each age is approximately 2,160 years, named for the constellation against which the vernal equinox rises during that period. Precession itself is an observable astronomical fact (Hipparchus, ~150 BCE); the assignment of project-historical events to specific ages is the corpus's working chronology.

ages.name: Age of Sagittarius
ages.headline: Atmospheric and oceanographic engineering; continents raised.

ages.name: Age of Scorpio
ages.headline: First synthesis of life; primary biosphere established.

ages.name: Age of Libra
ages.headline: Astronomical work; calibration of solar, lunar, and precessional motions.

ages.name: Age of Leo
ages.headline: The creation of humanity by seven factional teams.

ages.name: Age of Cancer
ages.headline: The Eden operation; exile of the makers; beginning of human history.

ages.name: Age of Aries
ages.headline: The Hebrew prophetic mission; most biblical history.

ages.name: Age of Pisces
ages.headline: Universal distribution of the message; major world religions take canonical form.

ages.name: Age of Aquarius
ages.headline: The age of disclosure. The current age.
